newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Interros-Oil wins Sidanko tender - Bank MFK.
newsitem.headline: Interros-Oil wins Sidanko tender - Bank MFK.

text.p: Russia's Interros-Oil won a tender for 51 percent of oil group SIDANKO with a $129.8 million bid, a spokesman for Bank MFK said on Friday.
Interros-Oil, affiliated with the Interros financial-industrial group built around Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), won an investment tender for 34 percent of SIDANKO in September last year.
Bank MFK, which is associated with Uneximbank, won control of the 51 percent stake under the government's shares-for-loans programme in December 1995 in return for a $130 million loan.
Russia's Federal Property Fund offered 118.53 million shares in SIDANKO, the 51 percent stake, at a starting price of $129.0 million.
OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years.
Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.

As winner of the tender, Interros-Oil must transfer within one month a further $100 million to SIDANKO to finance the development of oil exploration and production activities, and transfer a further $61 million within a year for the financial stabilisation of SIDANKO.
It must acquire if necessary and transfer to SIDANKO 73.70 million shares in the Angara refinery, in which SIDANKO already owns 38 percent, or 51 percent of the voting shares.
SIDANKO said at the end of December that it planned to issue convertible bonds and treble its authorised capital as part of a plan to consolidate shares of its subsidiaries into the parent.
It is also currently caught up in an ownership dispute over Purneftegaz with state-controlled Rosneft.
